summary: Lane County, OR lookout listed under the ODF Western Lane district: 40-ft tower with lookout house from 1949, station burned early 1972, 35-ft Aermotor tower erected 1972; now gone.

facts.design: 35-ft steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 cab (erected 1972); earlier 40-ft tower with 14x14 lookout house (1949)
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com and the FFLA index both list it as gone; no source describes what remains
facts.agency: Oregon Department of Forestry, Western Lane district (Western Lane FPA)

events.note: Construction began on a 14x14 standard lookout house on a 40-foot tower; materials cost $1,137.22
1950 report to the Oregon Department of Forestry gives the total cost of the improvement as $2,955.61
Portable tower under construction to replace the old tower; cabin to be stored at headquarters in winter; small trailer house for living quarters
Wolf Point lookout station burned to the ground during the winter; cause under investigation (Forest Log, January 1972)
35-foot steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 cab erected, with trailer house

evidence.supports: 1972 35-foot steel tower, 7x7 cab, trailer house; gone
evidence.quote: 1972: 35' steel tower w/ 7x7' cab, trailer house. Gone.

evidence.supports: Oregon Department of Forestry, Western Lane District
1949 construction of 14x14 lookout house on 40-foot tower
evidence.quote: Construction of a 14x14 standard lookout house on a 40 foot tower was begun
A total cost of the improvement was $2955.61.

evidence.supports: 1969 portable replacement tower, cabin stored at headquarters in winter
evidence.quote: Construction is in progress on a portable lookout tower to replace the old tower on Wolf Point. The tower will be constructed so the cabin is removed and brought to headquarters for storage in the winter.

evidence.supports: January 1972: station burned to the ground, cause under investigation
evidence.quote: Wolf Point Lookout Station in the Western Lane District burned to the ground this winter. The fire's cause was under investigation as this was written.
1972: A 35-foot steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 cab was erected.

evidence.supports: 1969: weather and vandalism reduced; small trailer house for living quarters
evidence.quote: This reduces weather deterioration and vandalism which is very common now. Living quarters are provided with a small trailer house.

corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) is the 1949 wooden tower. The steel Aermotor tower erected in 1972, which the record's design field names, is 35 ft (about 10.7 m) on both lists. Editor should confirm which structure the record describes.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 40 feet for the 1949 tower and 35 feet for the 1972 steel tower. The story treats the 1972 tower as the most recent one named in the sources.

notes_for_editor: The Forest Log item (January 1972) is quoted only through the Forest Lookouts page; we did not reach the original. Searches found nothing new about Wolf Point. The 1972 burn is reported without saying which structure burned. No staffing, fire, or current-site information found. The 1950 total covers the lookout and a storage garage.
